# attach

Upload a file as an attachment

## Synopsis

```
cdb attach <doc-path> <file> [flags]
```

## Description

Upload a file as an attachment.

## Arguments

Takes exactly 2 arguments.

## Flags

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--content-type` | string |  | content type, guessed from the file extension by default |
| `--name` | string |  | attachment name, defaulting to the file's base name |

## Global flags

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--anonymous` | bool | `false` | connect without credentials, and do not ask for any |
| `--color` | string |  | colour: auto, always or never |
| `--format` | string |  | output format: table or json |
| `--json` | bool | `false` | print raw JSON instead of a table |
| `--pager` | string |  | pager command, or off |
| `--path` | string |  | starting virtual path |
| `--profile` | string |  | connection profile to use, overriding CDB_PROFILE and the default |
| `--url` | string |  | server URL, overriding the profile and CDB_URL |
| `--verbose` | bool | `false` | include raw status codes and reasons in errors |
| `--yes` | bool | `false` | skip confirmation prompts |

## Examples

```
$ cdb attach /movies/tt0211915 ./poster.txt
Attached poster.txt (17 B) to /movies/tt0211915. The document is now at revision 5-ac866d9c221230c601e098ecae4e1c4d.

$ cdb attach /movies/tt0211915 ./cover.bin --name cover.png --content-type image/png
```
